title: The Farmers of Ur
description: We know from early clay tablets that temples in Mesopotamia distributed rations of grain to families for their field work. While the tablets only record genarlized quantities, we can imagine these families weighing their rations using shekels at the city market, deciding how to stretch their limited resources between barley — the staple grain on which they depended — and wool, needed to prepare clothing for the coming winter.
tradeoffs: How did ancient mesopatamia's view consumption? Was it really this or that?
